title: Thermochemical Pretreatment of Brewery Spent Grain: A Severity-Based Analysis of Hemicellulose Solubilization and Enzymatic Digestibility for  2G Ethanol
content: Brewery spent grain (BSG) is a strategic residual biomass for circular bioeconomy valorization. The typical chemical composition of large-scale industrial BSG and 2G-bioethanol theoretical yield estimations under operationally feasible conditions lie remarkably close to the minimum techno-economic feasibility requirements reported in the literature, making it a highly promising substrate to explore. Converting lignocellulosic biomass into bioethanol requires a multi-step process involving pretreatment, enzymatic saccharification, and fermentation. In this work, the thermochemical pretreatment of BSG using dilute H2SO4 was addressed as a structured tool to advance the understanding of biomass conditioning. A comprehensive analysis integrating thermal and chemical combined severity parameters with product release, biopolymer solubilization, cellulose digestibility, and process dynamics was performed using a central composite design and kinetic assays. Experimental factors and their interactions were thoroughly evaluated, revealing that a reduced quadratic model effectively described the variability of cellulose enzymatic hydrolysis at an initial time of 24 h. Notably, scarce literature reports full kinetic release data; here, hemicellulose solubilization reached 90-95% at intermediate severities, and conditioning at 15-16% w/v solid loading, 121 °C, 60 min, and 2.5% w/v H2SO4 yielded a cellulose recovery efficiency superior to 70%, with low generation of inhibitors (HMF, furfural, and acetate). To evaluate biological sugar utilization (glucose, xylose, and arabinose), non-detoxified BSG whole slurries were tested under various fermentation configurations (sequential and simultaneous) using non-conventional Spathaspora passalidarum NRRL Y-27907 and recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae TMB3400. Simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF) at 30 °C with S. cerevisiae TMB3400 achieved an ethanol concentration of 15.3 g/L at 72 h with 36% pentose removal, corresponding to a global process yield of 0.10 gethanol /gBSG. Finally, various strategies are discussed to enhance 2G-bioethanol implementation, highlighting the co-utilization of BSG and soybean hulls within a compatible operating window.
